subject.title: Manual context clearing for tool results

question: Should OpenClaw add caller-directed tool-result lifecycle control, and if so should it be destructive clear, recoverable archive, or active-context-only masking?
rationale: The request changes context/session semantics rather than fixing a broken existing contract, and current automatic pruning/truncation does not settle persistence, replay, authorization, or recovery behavior.

options.title: Design recoverable archive
options.body: Add a canonical archive/recover operation that removes selected tool results from active prompts while preserving auditable transcript state and explicit recovery.

options.title: Allow destructive clear
options.body: Expose a sharper clear operation that rewrites or elides selected tool results after defining who may call it and how replay/audit gaps are represented.

options.title: Keep automatic pruning only
options.body: Decline manual lifecycle control for now and rely on cache-TTL pruning, truncation, compaction, reset, and delete paths.

recommendation.title: Design recoverable archive
recommendation.body: Add a canonical archive/recover operation that removes selected tool results from active prompts while preserving auditable transcript state and explicit recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored cache-TTL pruning mode and is a high-confidence adjacent owner for the current automatic pruning behavior that this product decision would extend or replace.
